 Nomura has maintained its sum-of-the-parts (SOTP)-based target price of Rs 511 on Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles (TMCV), implying an upside of 27%, even as weak performance at subsidiary Iveco and a challenging commercial vehicle (CV) demand environment put the spotlight on execution. Tata Motors stocks were trading at Rs 427.30 on the NSE, up Rs 24.50 or 6.08% at 09:33 am. 
 In its November 4 report, titled 'Iveco's weak 3Q - TMCV's execution to be in focus', Nomura said demand and margin outlook had become tougher, with catalysts likely to be internal and significant potential for improvement under TMCV. Iveco reported a 1% year-on-year increase in revenue in the third quarter of calendar year 2026 (3QCY26), compared with 7% growth in the previous quarter. Overall volumes grew 7% year-on-year, against 11% in 2QCY26. However, industrial EBIT margin fell to zero in 3QCY26 from 2.8% in 2QCY26 and 2.5% in 3QCY25. Overall EBIT margin stood at 0.3%, compared with 3.2% sequentially and 2.9% a year earlier. By segment, truck revenue growth improved to 5% year-on-year, while bus revenue declined 6%. Industrial free cash flow (FCF) was negative EUR656 million in 3QCY26, against negative EUR513 million in 3QCY25 and negative EUR45 million in the preceding quarter. Order intake was largely flat, rising 1% year-on-year, with light-duty orders up 3% and medium- and heavy-duty orders up 2%. Bus order intake declined 24%. Margins and execution remain key monitorables 
 Nomura said Iveco's subdued performance continued, with margins under pressure amid a weak European CV market and macroeconomic uncertainties. "At the time of the acquisition, Iveco had guided for EBIT margins to improve from 5.4% in 2024 to 7.5% by 2028E. However, margins continue to track below our FY27F EBIT margin estimate of 2.8%," the brokerage said. With the acquisition now completed, Nomura expects integration synergies, including cost efficiencies and sourcing advantages, to support a gradual recovery in profitability over FY28F-29F. "Execution of cost optimization initiatives and the pace of earnings recovery remain key monitorables," it said. The brokerage added that the acquisition of Iveco would be funded through debt and internal accruals, and that TMCV did not need to raise equity. Nomura continues to value TMCV using an SOTP approach. It values the India CV business at 11 times average FY28-29F EBITDA, within its expected multiple band of 10-15 times, and maintains its target multiple for Iveco at four times CY28F EV/EBIT.
